name: mummer
summary: MUMmer 3.23 mummer (maxmat3): the maximal exact matches between a reference and query files, in the program's order.
short: MUMmer mummer: maximal exact matches (-mum / -mumreference / -maxmatch, -n -l -b -r -s -c -F -L), byte for byte.
description: MUMmer 3.23 mummer (Kurtz' maxmat3): the maximal exact matches between a reference file and one or more query files. matchMode 'mumreference' (default) reports matches unique in the reference, 'mum' matches unique in both, 'maxmatch' every maximal match; minLength = -l (default 20); nucleotidesOnly (-n) matches only a, c, g, t (any case); both (-b) adds the reverse-complement strand of the query, reverseOnly (-r) only that strand. Output per query record: a '> id' line and one line per match: reference position, query position, length (with several reference records or fourColumn = -F the reference id is the first column), followed by the matching text with showString (-s). Byte for byte equal to the installed mummer on 3 200 random runs (every mode, every option, multi-record files, N / IUPAC / odd characters, CR LF).

text: What mummer writes to standard output.
messages: The deterministic lines of standard error ('# reading input file ...'; the timing lines are left out).

errors: Sequence cannot be null or empty
At least one query file is required
matchMode must be 'mumreference', 'mum' or 'maxmatch'
mummer: empty sequence in multiple fasta file
mummer: option -b and option -r exclude each other

example.title: Maximal unique matches on both strands
example.prompt: Find the maximal unique matches of length >= 8 on both strands.

output.text:
> q
       1        14        20
acgtacgtacgtaaccggtt
> q Reverse
       1        10        13
acgtacgtacgta
      12         1         9
taaccggtt
output.messages:
# reading input file "reference.fa" of length 20
# construct suffix tree for sequence of length 20
# (maximum reference length is 536870908)
# (maximum query length is 4294967295)
# reading input file "query.fa" of length 34
# matching query-file "query.fa"
# against subject-file "reference.fa"

example.note: mummer -mum -l 8 -b -s r.fa q.fa: the whole reference matches the query at 14; the reverse-complement strand matches twice (the positions are in the reverse-complemented query).

name: promer
summary: MUMmer 3.23 promer: amino-acid alignments between two DNA files (six-frame translation, mummer, mgaps, postpro), the .delta file byte for byte.
short: MUMmer promer: six-frame amino-acid alignments (BLOSUM 45 / 62 / 80) of two DNA files, delta file byte for byte.
description: MUMmer 3.23 promer (PROtein MUMmer 3.07): amino-acid alignments between two multi-FASTA DNA files, the whole pipeline: prepro (six-frame translation, masking of short stop-to-stop stretches) | mummer on the translations | mgaps | postpro (the affine Smith-Waterman extension in amino-acid space with the BLOSUM matrix of matrix, give-up distance breakLength). Returns the .delta file (PROMER): coordinates of the original DNA, delta values in amino acids (one delta = three nucleotides); with delta = false the .cluster text; coords adds the PROmer 1.1 coords file; the temporary files of the script (.aaref, .aaqry, .mgaps) and the messages are returned too. Byte for byte equal to the installed promer on 320 recorded and 1 920 further random runs (every option).

delta: Text of the .delta file (null with delta = false).
cluster: Text of the .cluster file (only with delta = false).
messages: The progress lines of the script, the warnings of the programs and mummer's reading lines.
coords: Text of the coords file (only with coords = true).
aminoReference: The temporary .aaref file (the reference in six frames).
aminoQuery: The temporary .aaqry file (the query in six frames).

errors: Sequence cannot be null or empty
matchMode must be 'mumreference', 'mum' or 'maxmatch'
ERROR: mummer and/or mgaps returned non-zero
ERROR: Could not parse input from 'stdin'.

example.title: A gene with substitutions and an insertion
example.prompt: Align the two genes at the protein level.
example.note: promer -l 5 -c 10 ref.fa qry.fa: two alignments, forward in frame +3 (an insertion of two residues in the query: delta -51, -1) and on the reverse strand; the delta values count amino acids.

name: mummer_gaps
summary: MUMmer 3.23 gaps: the longest consistent set of matches, then the other matches, in mgaps format.
short: MUMmer gaps: longest consistent set of matches and the others (mgaps format), byte for byte.
description: MUMmer 3.23 gaps: reads a list of matches between two strings (start1 start2 length, as mummer prints them without the header lines; text that is not a number is refused - the program loops forever on it - and an empty list too - the program crashes) and prints first the longest consistent set of matches (ordered along both strings; overlaps are cut off: the overlap column shows the cut) after '> fileName [reverse] Consistent matches', then all the other matches after '> fileName [reverse] Other matches', in the format of mgaps: start1 start2 length overlap gap1 gap2 (the first line of a block has none - -; the other matches show a gap only after a match they chain to). Ties in the second start keep their input order. reverseComplement (-r) writes 'reverse' into the header lines, which mummer-annotate reads. Byte for byte equal to the installed gaps on 259 random match lists (+ the empty-list crash).

text: What gaps writes to standard output.

errors: Matches cannot be null or empty
gaps: the input contains '...': the program loops forever on text that is not a number.
gaps: no matches (the program dereferences a null array and crashes).

example.title: Consistent and other matches

output.text:
> g1.fa reverse Consistent matches
       3        9     20    none      -      -
      40       50     15    none     17     21
      70       80     30    none     15     15
> g1.fa reverse Other matches
      30       20      5    none      -      -

example.note: gaps g1.fa -r: three matches chain along both strings (gaps 17 / 21 and 15 / 15), the fourth is a match on its own.

name: delta2blocks
summary: MUMmer delta2blocks (Debian package): the alignments of a nucmer delta as lines with a CIGAR of M / X / I / D.
short: MUMmer delta2blocks: alignments of a nucmer delta file as CIGAR lines (M / X / I / D).
description: delta2blocks of the Debian MUMmer 3.23 package: the alignments of a nucmer delta file between one reference record and one query record as one line each, 'refId qryId sR eR sQ eQ CIGAR', the CIGAR written with M (matches), X (mismatches), I (an extra base in the reference, a positive delta) and D (an extra base in the query, a negative delta); the coordinates are those of the delta file (a reverse-strand alignment has sR > eR / sQ > eQ and is compared on the reverse complement). sortByReference (-r) / sortByQuery (-q) order the alignments. The sequences are read from the FASTA texts named in the delta header. A promer delta file is refused (the program reads the sequences through a null pointer and crashes). Byte for byte equal to the installed delta2blocks on 226 + runs.

text: What delta2blocks writes to standard output.
messages: What it writes to standard error.

errors: Delta file text cannot be null or empty
ERROR: Could not find any alignments for refId and qryId
delta2blocks: the program reads the sequences of a promer alignment through a null pointer and crashes (SIGSEGV).

example.title: Three substitutions
example.prompt: Give the CIGAR of the alignment.
example.note: delta2blocks d.delta ref qry: 65 matches, 2 mismatches, 1 match, 1 mismatch, 66 matches.

name: mummer_annotate
summary: MUMmer mummer-annotate: the edit-distance alignment of every gap of a gaps file, and witherrors.gaps.
short: MUMmer mummer-annotate: edit-distance alignment of the gaps of a gaps file with the error counts.
description: MUMmer 3.23 mummer-annotate (annotate): reads the output of gaps (the first sequence is named on its '>' lines - supply it in files by that name - and the word 'reverse' there reverse-complements the query), repeats the gap file and, under every gap line, prints the edit-distance alignment of the stretch between the two matches (10 bases of each flanking match included): '    Errors = n' and the rows 'T:' (first sequence) / 'S:' (query) / mismatch marks, 60 columns per block; a gap longer than 10 000 prints '*** Too long ***'. withErrors is the file witherrors.gaps the program writes: the gap lines with the number of errors appended. A window that reaches before the first base of a sequence reads memory in front of the program's buffer (valgrind: invalid read) and is refused with an error; beyond the end the buffer holds zeros. Byte for byte equal to the installed program on 230 + runs.

text: What mummer-annotate writes to standard output.

errors: Gap file text cannot be null or empty
Sequence cannot be null or empty
mummer-annotate: a gap window reaches before the first base of a sequence; ... (undefined behaviour).

example.title: Align the gap between two matches
example.prompt: Align the gap of this gaps file.

input.gaps:
> ref.fa  Consistent matches
       6        1     65    none      -      -
      75       70     66    none      4      4
> ref.fa  Other matches

output.text:
> ref.fa  Consistent matches
       6        1     65    none      -      -
      75       70     66    none      4      4
    Errors = 3
T:  cttaagggttaagtaagtgtgatg
S:  cttaagggttggggaagtgtgatg
              ^^ ^          
> ref.fa  Other matches
output.withErrors:
> ref.fa  Consistent matches
       6        1     65    none      -      -
      75       70     66    none      4      4       3
> ref.fa  Other matches

example.note: mummer-annotate g.gaps qry.fa: the gap between the two matches holds three substitutions.

name: run_mummer1
summary: MUMmer run-mummer1 script: mummer -mum -l 20 -r | gaps | mummer-annotate; returns .out, .gaps, .align, .errorsgaps.
short: MUMmer run-mummer1: mummer -mum -l 20 -r | gaps | mummer-annotate script, files .out .gaps .align .errorsgaps.
description: MUMmer 3.23 run-mummer1, the 'severely antiquated' script that runs the mummer 1 suite: mummer -mum -l 20 -r (reverse-complement matches only; the first output line is dropped) | gaps | mummer-annotate. reference and query are single-sequence FASTA texts; referenceName is the file name printed in the gaps file. Returns the files of the script: out (matches), gaps, align (the gaps with their alignments) and errorsGaps (the gaps with the number of errors). Without reverse (the script's fourth argument -r) the script passes an empty argument to mummer, which fails, and the tool refuses; a query with a second record makes gaps loop forever (refused), no match makes gaps crash (refused). Byte for byte equal to the installed script on 55 + runs.

errorsGaps: The gaps file with error counts (prefix.errorsgaps).

errors: Sequence cannot be null or empty
/usr/bin/mummer: cannot open file "" or file "" is empty (without -r ...)
gaps: no matches (the program dereferences a null array and crashes).
